name: Everest Helicopter Tour
alt_names: Everest Heli Tour with Kala Patthar Landing
sub_region: Kathmandu - Solukhumbu District, Koshi Province (Sagarmatha National Park)

difficulty.notes: No fitness needed, but passengers go from about 1,400 m to about 5,545 m within roughly 1.5 hours; ground time at Kala Patthar is limited to minutes because of altitude. Not advised for people with heart or lung conditions (consult a doctor).

duration_days.basis: Half-day, about 4-5 hours hotel to hotel
duration_days.notes: Morning departure for the clearest weather window. Private charter or shared seat. Can be combined with a trek (e.g. trek in, fly out from Gorak Shep).

max_altitude_point: Kala Patthar landing (weather and weight permitting); Everest Base Camp 5,364 m is overflown, not a sightseeing landing
start_point: Tribhuvan International Airport domestic terminal, Kathmandu

itinerary.route: Kathmandu - Lukla (refuel) - Pheriche (load shuttle) - overflight of Everest Base Camp - Kala Patthar landing - Hotel Everest View, Syangboche (breakfast) - Lukla - Kathmandu
itinerary.notes: Kathmandu-Lukla about 45 min; Lukla refuel 15-20 min; Kala Patthar ground time about 5-15 min; breakfast at Hotel Everest View (about 3,880 m) 30-60 min. In 2026 operators describe a Pheriche (about 4,371 m) shuttle, carrying passengers to Kala Patthar in small loads (two at a time) to respect weight limits.

best_seasons.notes: Clear mornings are most reliable in autumn and early winter; monsoon cloud causes frequent cancellations or shortened routes.

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park helicopter landing/hovering fee
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per landing (including hovering), charged per occasion to the operator

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry fee for heli passengers
permits.fee: Some operators include the NPR 3,000 park entry fee for passengers landing in the park; requirement for short landings not confirmed by an official source

guide_requirements: Not applicable (flight with pilot; operators assign a ground coordinator). Flights are run by CAAN-licensed helicopter operators.

flights: Helicopters commonly used: Airbus H125 / AS350 B3e (operator sources)
Kathmandu - Lukla about 45 min each way
Kala Patthar landing subject to weather and weight; at over about 5,500 m groups are split / shuttled (operator sources)
logistics.notes: Regulatory context: in December 2024 Sagarmatha NP and Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality ordered a halt to commercial heli flights from 1 January 2025; operators suspended flights from 5-6 January 2025. CAAN held that only the federal government regulates airspace. The park reversed its order; a 24 January 2025 stakeholder meeting allowed rescue flights, mountain flights with one-touch landings below 4,300 m, and expedition cargo to Pangboche. The municipality reimposed a ban on commercial flights above Lukla (except rescue, cargo and mountain flights) on 28 April 2025. Operators advertise shared Kala Patthar landings again in 2026. Confirm current status before each booking.

highlights: Close aerial views of Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam and the Khumbu Icefall
Overflight of Everest Base Camp and Khumbu Glacier
Landing at Kala Patthar facing Everest (when allowed)
Breakfast at Hotel Everest View with Everest panorama
Whole Everest experience in one morning
risks: Rapid altitude gain (hypoxia; very short ground time at Kala Patthar)
Weather cancellations, delays or shortened routes
Local Khumbu restrictions on commercial helicopter landings can change at short notice
Mountain flying risk (July 2023 Lamjura crash killed six people)

acclimatization.notes: No acclimatisation; exposure above 5,000 m kept to minutes.

unverified: 2026 status of Kala Patthar landings for shared tours: operators say resumed (one says from May 2026) via a Pheriche shuttle; no official CAAN or municipal notice found.
Whether the April 2025 municipal ban on commercial flights above Lukla was formally lifted or is simply not enforced.
Whether heli passengers must pay the Sagarmatha NP entry fee for short landings.
Kala Patthar height 5,545 m (GPS readings of about 5,644 m reported); landing pad sits slightly below the top.
Ground-time durations, Pheriche shuttle procedure and aircraft types are from operator sources only.
